newsitem.title: USA: St. Jude defibrillator approved by FDA.
newsitem.headline: St. Jude defibrillator approved by FDA.

text.p: St. Jude Medical Inc said Monday it received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for market release of a new model of the Ventritex Contour implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) for the ICD replacement market.
The new Contour model has two 6.1 millimeter high-voltage ports and two 5.0 millimeter sense/pace ports. It is designed to be compatible with early-generation defibrillation leads.

"The new Contour model represents another important addition to our ICD portfolio," Patrick Fourteau, president, St. Jude Medical Cardiac Rhythm Management Division, said in a statement. "We can now address the needs of many more patients with abnormally fast heart rhythms who are candidates for ICD replacement."
He said replacements account for more than 20 percent of ICD's implanted annually in the United States/
St. Jude develops, manufactures and distributes medical devices for the global cardiovascular market.
